translation: Mi ⟨se retuḥe⟩ ⟨en⟩ mi corazón ⟨y⟩ ⟨los⟩ terrores ⟨de⟩ la muerte ⟨han⟩ ⟨caído⟩ sobre mí

tokens.rationale: Hebrew יחיל properly means 'to twist or whirl'—here figuratively of the heart's torment; 'retorcerse' captures the physical metaphor better than 'angustiar'
אימות is from אֵמֶה (terror/dread) with plural suffix—literally 'terrors' (plural), not singular 'terror'
Hebrew perfect tense נפלו implies completed action—'fallen' (completed state), not 'falling' (ongoing)
